聖天子神謀宸斷旋復克平然無將之戒漸不
===
可長誠有如執事所慮者愚則以為幾者
事之微也古人於事不見是圖況其著乎
故幾之來也迎而治之則易為力蓋彼方
魁首倏吾之斷以下其張弛而吾之應之
賞功罰罪之典適以壓服其心厭是其意
不惟有以止亂而益成吾之治矣剏兩鎮
之變非有河北之從縣特以廩賜之不繼
勞逸之不均倡狂跳獗遂陷大戮然亦豈
聖世之所宜有哉故為今之計宜明賞罰之□
punctuated:
起於須臾，而應接失於倉卒，加之以武□解紐，制將非人，是以既乏先見之知，遂遺後事之悔耳。
國朝法令精明，軍政嚴肅，各省有都司，沿邊有諸鎮，兵皆土著，將則朝除。上有易制之權，下無世襲之患。如唐之河北諸鎮，萬萬無是。而近日甘肅、大同稍為不靖，賴我聖天子神謀宸斷，旋復克平。然無將之戒，漸不可長，誠有如執事所慮者。愚則以為幾者，事之微也。古人於事不見是圖，况其著乎？故幾之来也，迎而治之，則易為力。盖彼方翹首俟吾之斷，以卜其張弛，而吾之應之，賞功罰罪之典，適以壓服其心，厭足其意，不惟有以止亂，而益成吾之治矣。矧兩鎮之變，非有河北之桀黠，特以廩賜之不繼、勞逸之不均，倡狂跳踯，遂陷大戮，然亦豈聖世之所宜有哉？故為今之計，宜明賞罰之法。
translation_en:
…arose in an instant, and the response went awry in the haste of the moment. Added to this were the unraveling of military discipline [?; one character illegible] and the appointment of unsuitable men to control the generals. Thus, lacking the wisdom to foresee events, they merely left grounds for subsequent regret.
Our dynasty’s laws and ordinances are precise and clear, and its military administration is strict and orderly. Each province has a Regional Military Commission, and military commands are stationed along the frontier. The soldiers are all locally settled, while their commanders are appointed by the court. Above, the court possesses the authority to replace and control them; below, there is no danger of hereditary succession. Anything like the military commands of Hebei under the Tang is utterly out of the question. Recently, however, there has been some unrest in Gansu and Datong. Thanks to our sagely Son of Heaven’s inspired planning and imperial resolve, peace was soon restored. Yet the injunction against even contemplating rebellion must be heeded: incipient trouble must not be allowed to grow. There is indeed cause for the concern you have expressed.
In my humble view, an incipient sign is an event at its most subtle stage. The ancients took measures concerning affairs before they became apparent; how much more should one do so once they are manifest! Thus, when the first signs appear, meeting and dealing with them promptly makes the task easier. For those involved are then craning their necks, awaiting our decision, to gauge whether control will tighten or relax. If our response applies the established rules for rewarding merit and punishing offenses in a way that subdues their hearts and satisfies their wishes, we shall not only put an end to disorder but further perfect our governance.
Moreover, the disturbances in the two commands did not involve the fierce cunning of those in Hebei. It was simply because provisions and grants had fallen into arrears, and toil and ease were unevenly distributed, that the men ran wild and rose up, thereby bringing upon themselves the severest punishment. Yet how could such things properly occur in a sage’s age? Thus, in devising measures for the present, we should make clear the rules governing rewards and punishments…

title: 嘉靖四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
核功罪之當使太阿之柄常在
朝廷小過則黜大罪則刑而希冀無事因循
除拜如魏博之姑息不可也念付托之重
體征戍之勞而寵賂之章常防近習懷之
有恩遇之有道而誅求責望損重傷威如
承倩之將命不可也有野戰之勞則增其
品秩有拓地之勳則崇其爵土務使賞必
酬勞
恩常逾望如優游牽制而啓王武俊之邪謀
===
可乎有體統之嚴無壅蔽之患有擊斷之
威無讒譖之謀務使推心置腹銜恩效死
如隔絶排擯而致李懷光之怨望可乎抑
此皆即其事幾之來以圖其酬應之道若
探其本而論之則
朝廷者腹心也邊鎮者四肢也若
朝廷之上綱紀建立治化清明使其
恩如雨露其威如雷霆而奔走懾伏莫敢怠
玩然後大權操縱之下可以濟其幾之所

punctuated: 核功罪之當，使太阿之柄常在朝廷。小過則黜，大罪則刑，而希冀無事，因循除拜，如魏博之姑息，不可也。念付托之重，體征戍之勞，而寵賂之章，常防近習。懷之有恩，遇之有道，而誅求責望，損重傷威，如承倩之將命，不可也。有野戰之勞，則增其品秩；有拓地之勳，則崇其爵土。務使賞必酬勞，恩常逾望，如優游牽制而啓王武俊之邪謀，可乎？有體統之嚴，無壅蔽之患；有擊斷之威，無讒譖之謀。務使推心置腹，銜恩效死，如隔絶排擯而致李懷光之怨望，可乎？抑此皆即其事幾之來，以圖其酬應之道。若探其本而論之，則朝廷者腹心也，邊鎮者四肢也。若朝廷之上綱紀建立，治化清明，使其恩如雨露，其威如雷霆，而奔走懾伏，莫敢怠玩，然後大權操縱之下，可以濟其幾之所
translation_en:
…and scrutinize the proper assessment of merit and guilt, so that the hilt of Tai’a—the sword of sovereign authority—always remains in the hands of the court. Dismiss those who commit minor offenses and punish those who commit grave crimes. To hope that nothing will go wrong and continue making appointments by mere routine, indulging them as was done at Weibo, is unacceptable. Bear in mind the weight of the responsibilities entrusted to them and appreciate the hardships of campaigning and garrison service; constantly guard against close attendants becoming conspicuous through favors and bribes [?]. Win their allegiance through kindness and treat them according to proper principles. To make extortionate demands and exacting claims, diminishing the court’s dignity and damaging its authority, as Chengqian did when carrying out his mission, is unacceptable. For service in battle, raise their official rank; for achievements in extending the territory, enhance their titles and landed endowments. Ensure that rewards always recompense service and that imperial favor always exceeds expectations. Is it permissible to procrastinate and impose restraints, thereby prompting such treacherous designs as those of Wang Wujun?

Maintain strict hierarchical order without allowing communications to be obstructed; exercise the authority to act decisively without allowing slanderous plots. Ensure that trust is given wholeheartedly and that those who receive favor repay it with service unto death. Is it permissible to isolate and exclude them, thereby provoking such resentment as that of Li Huaiguang? Yet all these measures concern devising appropriate responses when the first signs of events appear. If we examine the root of the matter, the court is the heart and belly, while the frontier commands are the four limbs. If order and discipline are established at court and government and its transforming influence are clear and enlightened, so that its favor is like rain and dew and its might like thunder, and all hasten to serve in awed submission, none daring to be negligent or disrespectful, then, through the exercise of supreme authority, it will be possible to bring matters to a successful outcome as circumstances…

順天府鄉試錄後序
嘉靖乙酉秋八月甲午
上命學士臣鑾左贊善臣丕主順天
府試事翌日
陛辭入院三試之自丙申至丙辰

才以弼

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

On the jiawu day of the eighth month, in autumn of the yiyou year of Jiajing [1525], His Majesty ordered Academician Luan and Left Mentor Pi, his servants, to preside over the examination at Shuntian Prefecture. The following day, we took leave of His Majesty and entered the examination compound. We examined the candidates in three sessions, from the bingshen day through the bingchen day, twenty-one days in all, and the record was completed. It fell to me, your servant Pi, to write a postface for its closing pages.

I, your servant, had the undeserved distinction of becoming a provincial graduate here in the xinyou year of Hongzhi [1501]; twenty-four years have now elapsed. I had heard that the abundance of talent was twice what it had been formerly. Having recently come here under imperial command and had the opportunity to read all the candidates’ compositions, I find this indeed to be so. Yet I am without talent, and constantly fear that my discernment may lack precision and that I may fail to select men of true talent to assist this flourishing government. Nevertheless, the pledge I have made to myself is simply to devote my whole heart to the task. I humbly observe that those rulers of former ages who aspired to good government…

title: 嘉靖四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
未始不以求才為急務然心有
未純則好惡不得其正而舉措
失宜矣故必有恭默思道之君
而后獲帝賚之良必有側身脩
行之君而后獲嶽降之英非偶
然也恭惟
皇上紹正大統日以
===
敬天
法祖為事邇復
手諭輔臣緝熈
聖學是心也即文王純亦不已之
心也天下之以才自待而思欲
效用於時者固宜連茹而進而
况邦畿之士首被聲教者乎然

translation_en:
…have invariably regarded seeking talent as an urgent task. Yet if their hearts are not wholly pure, their likes and dislikes will not be rightly directed, and their appointments and dismissals will be inappropriate. Thus only with a ruler who reverently and silently contemplates the Way can a worthy bestowed by the Lord on High be obtained; only with a ruler who humbles himself and cultivates his conduct can an outstanding man sent down by the sacred mountains be obtained. This is no mere coincidence.
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty has succeeded to the rightful imperial line and daily devotes himself to revering Heaven and emulating the ancestors. Recently, Your Majesty again issued handwritten instructions to the chief ministers to further the cultivation and illumination of his sagely learning. This heart is precisely King Wen’s heart, whose purity likewise never ceased. Throughout the realm, those who esteem their own talents and wish to put them to use in the service of the age should surely advance together, like intertwined roots drawn up together. How much more so the scholars of the capital region, who are the first to receive the imperial moral influence and instruction! Yet …

title: 嘉靖四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
臣今日之所以鑒別其才與否
特以言耳是未敢信也言者心
之聲而文又言之精者則臣又
何敢弗自信以淺待諸士也哉
臣嘗驗之躁人之辭多中心疑

translation_en:
…the means by which your servant today distinguishes whether these men possess talent is merely their words; in this I have not dared place full confidence. Yet words are the voice of the heart, and writing is the finest expression of words. How, then, could your servant dare lack confidence in his own judgment and regard these scholars lightly? Your servant has repeatedly found this borne out: an impetuous man’s words are many; one who harbors doubts in his heart speaks in ramifying digressions; one who slanders the good speaks evasively; and one who has abandoned his principles speaks with embarrassment. It is invariably so.

Now, examining these scholars’ writings, I find neither verbosity nor digression, neither evasiveness nor embarrassment. All are indeed voices of the heart. By their outward expression one sees what lies within; through what is manifest one discerns what is subtle. Thus, when they come forward to serve the needs of the age, they will surely be able to remain content in their circumstances and await their time, without erring through impetuosity. Seeing what is right, they will act, without erring through doubt. They will maintain impartiality in judging right and wrong without distorting the facts, and heed the admonition to be watchful from beginning to end without wavering in their integrity. text:
弼成
嘉靖之治則我
皇上純心之效於是乎大矣事竣將
陛見對揚
休命執此藉手諸士幸相與勉之勿
他日為才所使與先資之言異
以重主司之羞

punctuated:
弼成嘉靖之治，則我皇上純心之效於是乎大矣。事竣，將陛見，對揚休命，執此藉手。諸士幸相與勉之，勿他日為才所使，與先資之言異，以重主司之羞。
左春坊左贊善謝丕謹序。
translation_en:
…to assist in perfecting the governance of the Jiajing reign: then the effects of our Emperor’s purity of heart will indeed be great. With the examination concluded, I shall have an imperial audience and gratefully acknowledge His gracious commands, presenting this as evidence of their fulfillment. May you gentlemen encourage one another in this endeavor. Do not someday let yourselves be driven by your talents and depart from the foregoing words [?], thereby adding to the shame of the presiding examiner.
Preface respectfully written by Xie Pi, Left Assistant Adviser of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
